source.title: dnaHNet: A Scalable and Hierarchical Foundation Model for Genomic Sequence Learning
source.authors: Arnav Shah; Jun-Zhe Li; Parsa Idehpour; Adibvafa Fallahpour; Brandon Wang; Sukjun Hwang; Bo Wang; Patrick D. Hsu; H. Goodarzi; Albert Gu

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in genomic sequence models, an application beyond text pretraining, and reports scaling and downstream results.
record.gate_note: The paper reports evaluation-perplexity scaling fits, compute-matched comparisons, an optimal-token comparison, and downstream metrics across compute budgets. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results. It says optimal model sizes and token counts were computed for each budget, but does not give the numerical series or fitted allocation exponents.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of evaluation perplexity against training compute for three genomic sequence model families (over 100 runs, 10M–1B parameters, 4e18–8e19 FLOPs). It also reports Chinchilla-style optimal token counts and downstream zero-shot metrics across compute budgets. This is a new modality (prokaryotic DNA) with its own results, so it bears on V5, V6 and V7. V3 is touched only weakly.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that dnaHNet scales more compute-efficiently than StripedHyena2 and Transformers (α 0.06 vs 0.04 vs 0.01), with a widening gap. They also find its compute-optimal regime uses more tokens than Chinchilla-style laws applied to raw nucleotides predict: 140B vs StripedHyena2's 68B at 8e19 FLOPs. They attribute this to compression. They note scaling was tested only up to 1B parameters.
record.recipe_differences: Uses established scaling-law and Chinchilla-style analysis, but applies it to genomic pretraining, hierarchical architectures, and evaluation perplexity; it does not report small-run extrapolation tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported compute-scaling exponent varies by architecture family; the paper also states that the optimal data-to-parameter ratio differs from standard non-hierarchical scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched compute, dnaHNet's perplexity advantage over StripedHyena2 widens from 0.078 to 0.118 points between 8e18 and 6e19 FLOPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture comparisons at matched compute: hierarchical compression architectures gain an efficiency advantage that grows with compute.

record.problems: The scaling analysis extends only to 1B parameters and prokaryotic pretraining. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the extracted results. The optimal allocation comparison gives one compute-budget example rather than the numerical allocation trend across budgets.

untested.parts: Not text language models. No separate parameter- or token-limited fits.
No fitted law is checked against a much larger run. The 3e20 FLOPs figure for SH2 is an unverified extrapolation.
No allocation exponents or optimal N and D series across budgets are reported.
No depth or width variation at fixed parameter count. Hierarchy-stage comparisons are qualitative only.
Only genomic autoregressive pretraining is tested. No images, video, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer. Compute range is about 1.3 orders of magnitude, not several.
No fitted downstream law and no relation to pretraining loss; only monotone trends versus compute.
Fitting method, parameter counting, schedule and data are not varied, and curvature away from a power law is not examined.

missing.what: Compute-optimal model sizes at 8e19 FLOPs: dnaHNet 218M vs StripedHyena2 166M parameters. These conflict with the text's 'proportionally larger model' for SH2.
An extrapolated claim that SH2 would need 3e20 FLOPs to match dnaHNet's perplexity at 8e19 (3.75x). It is derived from the fits and is not verified by a run.
The statement that the optimal dnaHNet token count grows 'without plateauing', and that optimal N and D were computed for every budget but not reported.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its V3 evidence is a single budget, with a parameter-count statement that conflicts with Figure 2, so no V3 verdict is given. Exponents are on perplexity rather than loss, and no uncertainty is reported. The 1-, 2- and 3-stage dnaHNet variants appear pooled in the fit.

versions.untested_parts: The tested systems model genomic sequences, not the held-out pretraining loss of language models described by this version; the paper reports evaluation perplexity versus compute, not separate parameter- and token-scaling fits.
No test of predictions from small-run fits against runs orders of magnitude larger is reported.
The paper gives an optimal-token comparison at one stated compute budget, but not numerical optimal parameter and token counts across budgets or fitted growth exponents for either.
No test isolating effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
Tests genomic pretraining on prokaryotic sequences; does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Reports downstream metrics versus training compute, not their relationship to pretraining loss.

Reports differences in compute-scaling exponents across architecture families and an optimal-token comparison, but does not vary parameter-counting, fitting method, data, or training schedule systematically, nor report curve bending away from a single power law.

relationships.condition: dnaHNet and StripedHyena2 genomic models, 4e18–8e19 FLOPs
relationships.reason: Perplexity follows a fitted PPL = A·C^−α with α = 0.06 and 0.04 (R1, R2), though over only about 1.3 decades and with no reported fit quality.
relationships.display_finding: Perplexity fit compute power laws with exponents 0.06 for dnaHNet and 0.04 for StripedHyena2 over approximately 1.3 orders of magnitude, without reported fit quality.

source_check.reason: Section 4.3 reports PPL = A·C^−α with exponents 0.06 and 0.04 over the stated compute range. Evidence is limited to evaluation perplexity, with no numerical fit-quality assessment.

relationships.reason: The fitted exponent is only α = 0.01, so perplexity is nearly flat across a 20x compute range (R3).
relationships.display_finding: The fitted exponent was α=0.01, leaving perplexity nearly flat across a twentyfold compute range.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Section 4.3 reports the same fitted power-law form for Transformers, with α = 0.01. V5 specifies the functional form, without a minimum exponent; slow improvement alone does not establish a failure of that form.

relationships.condition: dnaHNet and StripedHyena2 on MaveDB VEP and DEG essentiality
relationships.reason: Spearman and AUROC rise monotonically with training FLOPs in every dnaHNet and SH2 series (R7–R14, R19–R30). SH2 flattens at its top budget, and no fitted predictive law is given.
relationships.display_finding: Spearman correlation and AUROC rise monotonically with training FLOPs in every series, although StripedHyena2 flattens at its highest budget and no predictive law is fitted.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Table 5 reports Spearman 0.1348, 0.1355, 0.1497, and 0.1555 across increasing budgets. The improvement is small, particularly over the first 2.5-fold compute increase, consistent with partial scaling rather than absence.

relationships.display_finding: Compute exponents were 0.06, 0.04 and 0.01 across architectures, and hierarchical models departed from Chinchilla's optimal data ratio at the single tested budget.
